{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZjLRkw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDJ6XY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 81, "title": "Correct zero-pitch S-DSP terminal-header muting after KON", "body": "## Problem

At evaluation baseline `f4ca3ce3d8c10850da72924e0926ec5f40b2a68d`, initial BRR terminal-header handling depends on pitch consuming a nibble. A newly keyed voice with pitch zero therefore never recognizes header flags `01`, leaving its envelope active and potentially making NON-selected noise audible indefinitely.

In [dsp.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f4ca3ce3d8c10850da72924e0926ec5f40b2a68d/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L65-L83), header loading and zero-envelope/release selection occur inside `decode`. `sample` calls that function only when pitch advancement crosses an integer interpolation position. Initial pitch `$0001` likewise postpones recognition until its first nibble demand.

This is an incomplete edge of Issue #79, prioritized by the latest assessment. That improvement covered nonzero pitches `$1000/$1800/$3000`; its [tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f4ca3ce3d8c10850da72924e0926ec5f40b2a68d/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_brr_end.rs) do not exercise zero-pitch terminal recognition. No duplicate open Issue is present in the supplied context.

## Expected outcome

For a directory entry and initial BRR block stable before KON and throughout initialization, recognize the initial terminal header independently of interpolation demand. Header `01` must force envelope zero and release even at pitch zero and regardless of NON. Increasing pitch or changing envelope registers afterward must not revive that released voice; a new KON can initialize it again.

### Hardware contract and evidence

The repository's [Issue #79 source reconciliation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/f4ca3ce3d8c10850da72924e0926ec5f40b2a68d/docs/issue-79-validation.md#source-reconciliation) records these distinctions:

- [Anomie/jwdonal S-DSP documentation, revision 1212](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0#file-apudsp_jwdonal-txt), SOUND GENERATION S3b/S3c/S4 and BRR DECODING, separates header handling from demand-driven decoding. Header flags `01` select release with zero envelope. Muting does not stop internal processing.
- [Fullsnes, BRR Samples, Loop/End bits](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesapudspbrrsamples) distinguishes sequential flags `00/10`, terminal `01`, and looping `11`. NON substitutes the audio source before envelope scaling; it does not exempt a voice from terminal-envelope silence.
- [Shay Green/blargg's pinned research implementation](https://github.com/snes9xgit/snes9x/blob/8028d3b6ca994f21fdff220d513a08382e37afc3/apu/bapu/dsp/SPC_DSP.cpp), V3b/V3c versus V4, corroborates header reading and terminal-envelope handling separately from interpolation-demand decoding. V4–V7 distinguish block-end detection from ENDX publication. Use this as attributed research evidence, without importing implementation code or emulator-generated expected results.

These external links are citations already recorded in the repository; they were not fetched during this repository-only assessment. The recorded distinction supports correcting indefinite pitch-gated header omission. It does not establish an exact physical prefetch or register-publication schedule.

For this bounded scalar API correction, retain the existing five silent KON calls and require the initial terminal voice to have zero PCM/ENVX/OUTX by the first subsequent ordinary sample call. Document that boundary as an API mapping, not a physical subcycle measurement. Header recognition alone must not report block completion through ENDX or artificially advance pitch to manufacture a fetch.

### Scope and non-goals

Implement initial stable-header recognition after KON, including zero and very low pitch, terminal release persistence, voice isolation, and later resumption of silent BRR/end processing when pitch advances.

Do not implement a complete lookahead pipeline, ordinary zero-pitch BRR waveform preloading, live BRR-header edits, changes racing KON, torn directory/pitch writes, DSP subcycles, SPC bus scheduling, firmware execution, frontend changes, or unrelated refactoring. Keep PMON disabled in the new discriminating vectors; this Issue does not resolve the separately documented NON/PMON progression dispute.

## Context and reproduction

Use an original public-API fixture based on `dsp_brr_end.rs::setup`:

1. Place an original filter-0 BRR block at `$3000`, referenced by DIR `$20`, SRCN zero. Give it nonzero signed payload and header low bits `01`; keep its loop target distinct.
2. Configure pitch `$0000`, direct GAIN 64, NON bit 0 enabled, FLG `$20` (noise rate zero, echo writes disabled), voice volumes `64/-128`, master volumes `64/64`, and zero echo contribution. Issue KON for voice 0.
3. Sample through the five silent KON calls and beyond.

Static derivation of current behavior: held noise seed `$4000` gives signed source `-32768`; GAIN 64 gives envelope 1024. The sixth call therefore produces PCM `(-4096, 8192)`, ENVX 64 and OUTX 192, because `decode` never reads the terminal header. Required terminal output is PCM `(0,0)`, ENVX/OUTX `(0,0)`, with release retained. The same numerical noise output is a useful positive control for initial header flags `00`, `10`, and `11` under this retained API convention.

This reproduction is source-derived, not an executed test result. The working tree was clean and HEAD matched the supplied baseline; no suites were rerun during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add original public-API tests in `crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_brr_end.rs` covering all four initial header flags, pitches `$0000` and `$0001`, direct GAIN and fast ADSR, and NON enabled/disabled. Check PCM, ENVX, OUTX and ENDX at explicit boundaries. Terminal recognition must occur before the first pitch-driven nibble demand. NON-enabled nonterminal controls must retain independently calculated audible output, rejecting a blanket zero-pitch mute workaround.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the zero-pitch terminal/NON discriminator fails behaviorally on the unmodified evaluation baseline and passes after the production correction. Record commands and actual values; compilation failures and agreement between emulator runs are not hardware evidence. Expected values must come from attributed semantics and independent arithmetic, not production helpers or captured emulator output.
- [ ] Test release persistence across GAIN/ADSR edits, NON toggles, and pitch changes `$0000 → $1000 → $0000`. Check that raising pitch permits continued silent processing, live end-bit redirection, and later ENDX clear/reassert behavior. During the initial zero-pitch hold, header recognition alone must leave ENDX clear. Include ordinary KOFF, a subsequent KON selecting a distinct nonterminal start block, and an unaffected second voice. Use justified scalar boundary counts without claiming physical fetch timing.
- [ ] Add an original SPC700 guest uploaded through the existing firmware-free protocol. The guest must configure zero pitch/NON/terminal data through `$F2/$F3`, record ENVX/OUTX/ENDX in RAM, and exercise pitch change and retrigger controls. Require bounded acknowledgements and completion, independently expected register/PCM checkpoints, and whole-versus-irregular `Apu::tick` comparisons of every PCM sample, all DSP registers, RAM and output ports. Equality establishes determinism only.
- [ ] Document original guest/vector authorship and MIT provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`. Update the validation record and relevant README limitations to explain the corrected initial-header behavior, source reconciliation, baseline failure, actual checks, and remaining uncertainties. Supersede any earlier assumption that header visibility requires nibble consumption; do not retain unsupported expectations solely because an earlier Issue used them.
- [ ] Pass the following Rust checks, retaining existing BRR-end, directory, noise, pitch, envelope, mixing, echo and other workspace regressions:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_brr_end
cargo test --workspace --locked
```

- [ ] Pass the existing README source-built hardware and browser gates before merge, using the documented toolchain override where needed:

```sh
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
(cd web && npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds')
```

Preserve licensed fixture source pins, provenance, expected hashes, and existing Castle/Memory replay durations, routes, freeze controls, gameplay assertions, numerical audio and live Web Audio checks. No commercial ROM or firmware acquisition is required. Report every mandatory result accurately; unperformed checks are not passes.

- [ ] Preserve all 24 inventory categories and their full supplied scopes/outstanding work. Partial: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing`. Unimplemented: `ppu-raster`, `pal`. None becomes verified. Specifically retain unresolved physical KON/header lookahead and publication timing, live-header sampling, directory/key races, reset retention, independent BRR-filter 1–3 evidence, exhaustive interpolation phases and simultaneous-key combinations. Passing these bounded tests establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility and does not complete Issue #3.

None.

None.
